title: Decompose Coulomb heat collision terms without a divergent weight average
statement: For fixed tau>0 let p_tau(y)=P_tau F(y), mu_y(dx)=K_tau(y,x)F(x)dx/p_tau(y). The exact truncated term is B_tau=int p_tau Cov_mu(q,alpha q)dy. For independent x,xprime under mu, (q-qprime)(alpha q-alpha_prime qprime)=(sqrt(alpha)q-sqrt(alpha_prime)qprime)^2-(sqrt(alpha)-sqrt(alpha_prime))^2 q qprime. Thus B is one HALF the integrated nonnegative score square minus one HALF an explicit radial commutator. At fixed tau with the stated profile integrability, score-retaining moments alpha q^2 and |alpha q| control these terms without E_mu alpha, which generally diverges. The equivalent two-point kernel F(x)F(xprime)int K_tau(y,x)K_tau(y,xprime)/p_tau(y)dy is state-dependent; an unweighted translation-invariant Hardy estimate cannot be imported automatically. Generic positivity fails on two equal atoms alpha=(1,4),q=(2,1): Cov=-1/2 and the square vanishes. This is NOT a physical product-score negative certificate or global-Cauchy obstruction. Heat endpoint domination, physical-time differentiation and an integrated growth/sign bound remain OPEN.
